newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Charts sour for copper below $2,500.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Charts sour for copper below $2,500.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper's failure to hurdle key resistance at $2,500 suggests further weakness on Thursday, analysts said. A breach of nearby support could target $2,440.
Aluminium looks brighter on the charts after a positive close on Wednesday, but remains vulnerable to further selling pressure as long as prices remain below $1,600.
COPPER - A break below $2,470 support on Wednesday and failure to bounce back above key resistance at $2,500 leaves copper vulnerable to further losses, analysts said.
Support levels were seen at $2,460 and then $2,440-$2,445.
"Copper...closed at 7 p.m. on Tuesday's low at $2,467/70, suggesting a test of $2,461 and if broken falls to $2,445 and lower," said analyst Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading Ltd.
The 14-day RSI was at 58 after being in overbought territory above 70 at the start of the week.
A rise in copper stocks on Wednesday, along with a softening backwardation were also helped undermine prices.
The strike at Inco Ltd's Sudbury copper and nickel operations had yet to excite the market, although signs of a long stoppage could eventually lend support to the market, analysts said.
AT 0945 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,466/$2,474 per tonne, down from $2,478 at Thursday's kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - A strong close on Wednesday suggests aluminium could try to hurdle to $1,600 resistance level in the near term, especially as recent fund selling has appeared to ease off, analysts said.
"A rally back above $1,605 would send a signal that the recent downwave was a bear trap," brokers GNI said in a commentary.
In contrast to copper, LME stocks fell solidly on Wednesday and more drops this week would boost aluminium's case.
Three months metal was last indicated at $1,592/$1,594 per tonne, versus $1,592 at Thursday's close.
